messages:
maria: Heads-up — experimenting with an 'opportunistic' GPU queue to squeeze cost from spot instances without tanking interactive latency. Thinking: short interactive sessions (<=60s) go to opportunistic queue with soft preempt, and batch jobs stay on reserved. Any concerns?

ashok: Quick q — what do you mean by 'soft preempt'? time-windowed evictions or graceful drain?

maria: Soft preempt = give interactive jobs a small grace window and try warm-fallback to local quantized model or CPU for last 1-2 tokens if eviction imminent. Avoid full context loss.

jen: Love the idea. We need explicit knobs: eviction_budget_seconds, max_queue_wait_ms, and a QoS class. Example config snippet:

```yaml
queue: opportunistic-interactive
  priority: 50
  preempt_policy: soft
  eviction_budget_seconds: 10
  max_session_length_seconds: 60
  fallback_path: quantized-cpu
```

jen: Also add a max_retries=1 so we don't spin a request across zones too much.

dave: On infra side, two thoughts: 1) autoscaler must treat this queue as burstable — scale with spot supply signals, not demand alone. 2) Off-peak shift window to tilt more weight to opportunistic (00:00-06:00 local) per region. Helps cost when traffic is low.

maria: Good call on regional windows. We should also set sticky-affinity for chat KV cache for ~30s to reduce rewarm cost when we fall back. Not losing the session is critical for UX.

lina: Need fairness rules too — interactive should have small tokens budget so batched training doesn't hog opportunistic pool. Maybe per-team credits that replenish daily.

ops-bot: rollout-stats: {"opportunistic_pool_nodes":48, "current_spot_interrupt_rate_pct":3.1, "p95_latency_ms_now":280, "spot_savings_pct":21} :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ashok: For fallback we can expose a tiny quantized 1.5B CPU path that returns last-k tokens while we requeue the full GPU job. Cheap and fast in most cases.

jen: caution — some features (tool-calls, large context) can't be safely truncated. We'll need request classifiers that opt-out (header: X-OPPORTUNISTIC-OK: true).

dave: Rollout plan proposal: canary 5% of interactive traffic (region A), watch p99 and error-rate for 48h. If stable, 25% next week. Metric gates: p99 <= baseline+30ms, success_rate >= 99.5%.

maria: +1 to canary. I'll add the classifier and header. Also will add a per-request flag to force reserved execution (X-RESERVED-PIN: true) for enterprise customers.

lina: Ops question — how do we surface eviction reasons to customers? We should include a bit in response metadata like `{"served_from":"opportunistic","evicted":true,"evict_reason":"spot_interruption"}` so SDKs can handle gracefully.

ashok: yep, response headers or top-level meta is best. SDK can auto-retry with reserved if evicted and user allows.

jen: Also log trace_id->node_id mapping so we can reconstruct where context was lost for debugging.

ops-bot: perf-alert: simulated off-peak run shows 18-24% cost reduction with p99 latency regression of ~12ms in our model mix.

maria: OK action items: (1) jen — add classifier + config schema, (2) dave — autoscaler rules + regional off-peak toggle, (3) ashok — implement quantized CPU fallback path, (4) lina — crediting/fairness policy sketch, (5) ops-bot — add eviction metadata to responses. I'll create a 30-min sync tomorrow 10:00 PT to align rollout gates.

dave: I'll prep the canary dashboard (p50/p95/p99, errors, interrupt-rate, cost-savings).

jen: will draft schema PR later today.

maria: Thanks all — let's keep the initial canary narrow and observable. If we hit any surprising QoS drops we roll back fast. :thumbsup:
